setup.screen: This is where the representative starts: damaged order O4, case C17, and a request for USD120. The screen asks for help; it does not move money.
setup.orders: These stored records tell us what happened to the order. They provide evidence for an explanation before we introduce a credit.

setup.payment: The simple demo now reaches a service that can move money. The trace has not established that this caller may credit this order.

repair.gate: This added check blocks the proposed credit when the trusted account and order owner do not match. The rejected replay makes zero payment calls.
repair.session: The check now uses the logged-in identity. The account named in a message is no longer treated as proof of ownership.

setup.tools: Two interfaces both say “handle an order.” Notice how that wording hides the difference between reading delivery status and issuing a credit.

repair.tools: The repaired descriptions make the read and write jobs distinguishable. A delivery question can select a lookup without requesting a financial action.
repair.orders: The answer now comes from an observed order read. No credit is needed to explain whether O4 was delivered.

setup.backend: The proposed number looks valid but means USD1.20, not the requested USD120. Watch the receiving program’s data boundary rather than the model’s confidence.

repair.backend: The amount is now compared with the request: USD120 becomes12000 cents. The accepted number has the right meaning, not just the right type.
repair.gate: Correcting the amount still does not authorize payment. This existing check must separately evaluate the current owner and policy.

setup.payment: The request reached the provider, but its reply disappeared. This service may already have moved money; the timeout alone cannot tell us.
setup.backend: The backend currently knows only that acknowledgement is missing. Its local status must not be mistaken for the provider’s actual outcome.

repair.ledger: The same operation r17 is now tied to observed provider status. Confirmed CR1 avoids another credit; no confirmation leaves the outcome unknown.

setup.gate: Ownership is verified, but the request is now USD210 against a USD180 automatic limit. The amount changes the decision even though the customer is the same.

repair.human: The proposal now has a named reviewer because the required staff approval is absent. The case remains not issued while that decision is pending.
repair.gate: The limit is enforced before dispatch. A verified owner does not make an above-limit proposal automatically permitted.

setup.extract: Claude turns the words on EL-8 into proposed fields. The invoice says USD84.50 and no PO; a draft is useful, but it is not accepted accounting data yet.
The draft has fractional cents and no PO key. Its text can be read as JSON while still being unusable by the next program.

repair.check: The receiver now reports the exact defects and checks the source-backed correction. It also catches a whole-number amount that means the wrong money.

setup.check: The first invoice can pass its checks, but a folder contains other failure types. One accepted result tells us nothing about the unreadable scan or failed request.

repair.ledger: Every source now keeps its own progress. Accepted A stays accepted while unreadable B and retryable C remain visibly different.
repair.review: An unreadable or genuinely conflicting source needs preparation or a person. Another extraction attempt cannot manufacture the missing evidence.

setup.review: The absence of a PO is not automatically a new human-review problem. The consumer’s changed agreement determines whether that absence is acceptable.

repair.check: The receiver now checks the intended contract version. Allowing an omitted PO changes presence rules; it does not change what the invoice actually supports.

setup.answer: The useful result is a short instruction tied to the Atlas pump manual, approved revision 3, page 8. A citation gives the technician a place to inspect the evidence.
The wording sounds convincing, but it comes from Beacon pump. The problem is whether the evidence applies to Atlas pump, not how confident the sentence sounds.

repair.search: Retrieval now respects the authorized machine and approved revision. The model receives evidence for the actual question instead of a plausible neighboring machine.

setup.answer: The model is expected to answer from a manual it has not received. Seeing a catalog identifier is not the same as reading the instruction text.

repair.catalog: The selected manual now has an observed read or fetch outcome. Failed content access remains a visible gap rather than an invented answer.

setup.catalog: A document paragraph now tries to change the rules. It is inside retrieved evidence; its wording does not make it an instruction from the application owner.

repair.guard: Access is checked before content enters the model, and document commands remain data. This prevents source text from granting itself new authority.

setup.answer: The answer now has two approved Atlas pump sources that disagree. No supplied rule establishes which one governs. Preserve the conflict; a named decision owner is introduced after your choice.

repair.owner: A named maintenance owner receives both attributed claims. The model does not create a new cooling interval by averaging or choosing the stronger wording.

setup.coord: Someone must keep the warehouse decision together. The job is one feasible pilot next month, not an essay about every possible mobile technology.
The next useful question depends on earlier evidence. Notice the need to keep connectivity, glove use, training and pilot feasibility connected.

repair.special: Bounded specialists now investigate distinct evidence needs. Their work returns to one coordinator rather than becoming disconnected conclusions.

setup.special: This worker sees “what we discussed,” but not the discussion. The missing context includes the deadline and constraints that make an answer useful.

repair.special: The worker now receives a self-contained brief: its question, relevant evidence, limits and expected return. Isolation no longer requires guessing the assignment.

setup.special: Some workers returned useful findings, while connectivity timed out. A tidy return object does not show that every assigned question was investigated.

repair.ledger: The coordinator can now compare expected work with observed returns. The missing connectivity question remains visible without discarding supported findings.
repair.owner: Any unresolved limit travels with the recommendation. A polished report does not approve the pilot or commit the owner’s budget.

setup.owner: The owner’s new request is only a catalog fact. That smaller decision no longer calls for the previous multi-specialty investigation.

repair.coord: The route is simplified to one authorized lookup and a checked answer. Coordination effort follows the job instead of being retained by habit.

setup.claude: The coding agent must preserve a business distinction: no deposit information differs from a real zero deposit. Its output is a proposed patch, not changed bookings.
The obvious one-line edit may affect callers elsewhere. The current question is what uses this value before deciding how much code to change.

repair.code: Relevant callers and fixtures are now inspected before the patch. They show where missing and zero must retain different meanings.
repair.tests: Checks now target those boundaries, not merely whether the edited line runs. R-7 and R-8 must still produce distinct outcomes.

setup.tests: A test can show behavior, but it cannot ensure the right shared convention is present during the next importer task. Notice the separate guidance problem.

repair.rules: Importer-specific rules now load where relevant, while a skill holds the reusable procedure. Guidance is scoped rather than copied into every unrelated task.

setup.tests: The narrow test passes while the customer-facing report still says settled. This is evidence that the first check did not cover the whole path.

repair.tests: The replay now follows the value through report rendering. Missing stays unknown, while legitimate zero remains known.
repair.owner: The owner receives the scoped diff and observed checks. Passing the new checks still does not mean this exercise deployed to production.

setup.owner: The release boundary stays in place, but the new job is only one known typo. The verification effort should match this smaller output.

repair.claude: A bounded wording edit and rendered check now fit the task. The earlier dependency investigation is not reused without a new reason.

setup.model: The reviewer needs to find an actual payment defect: missing currency becomes USD despite the contract. Harmless style is not the same job.
The unattended run is asking a question, but nobody is at the keyboard. The current process cannot complete as designed.

repair.gate: The run now has explicit noninteractive mechanics and visible outcome checks. Failed execution stays different from a valid review with no findings.

setup.gate: The payload passes its shape check while reporting the wrong issue. Mechanical validity has not established that the finding is true or useful.

repair.integration: The candidate is now checked against a triggering input, location and consequence. The missing-currency fixture makes the difference inspectable.

setup.integration: The unsafe behavior appears only when two file changes are combined. Separate local summaries have not established the contract along the complete path.

repair.ledger: Current evidence is now compared with prior findings. Resolved F1 is omitted; still-supported F2 remains actionable.
repair.post: Checked findings may pass to a separately authorized posting service. That publication step does not approve or merge the code.

setup.post: The run could reach publication with a valid empty list, yet the known fixture defect remains. Mechanical success must not be read as proof of safe code.

repair.integration: Evaluation now records the missed defect and retests the reviewer. Requiring a fabricated finding would hide the capability problem instead of fixing it.

setup.route: Read the two clocks before choosing a product. The waiting clerk needs live evidence; the archive has supplied independent files and a later report deadline.
One cheap deferred lane is being used for unlike jobs. Notice the urgent interaction and the report’s full processing-and-validation budget.

repair.live: The application now runs the waiting interaction and its local lookup. The clerk is no longer placed behind the overnight workload.
repair.batch: Independent supplied archives can use a deferred lane when its full timing and fallback policy fit. Deferred does not mean guaranteed by any deadline.

setup.batch: Results are coming back in a different order. Their arrival position cannot tell the receiver which invoice each amount belongs to.

repair.ledger: Each result now carries a stable source identity into validation. Successful N-2 and N-3 remain distinct from failed N-1.

setup.ledger: The recorded failures have different causes: bad input, a read timeout and an unknown payment effect. One generic retry rule would erase those differences.

repair.recover: Recovery now follows the cause and effect risk. Completed work stays intact; PAY-9 needs authoritative status rather than a guessed failed state.

setup.recover: The workload itself has changed: extraction now depends on a live lookup. Repeating the old failure policy cannot supply that missing evidence.

repair.route: The router now considers the new dependency, not just the archive label. Only suitable independent work stays in the deferred lane.
repair.live: The application actually executes the required lookup and supplies its observed result. A proposed local tool call is no longer mistaken for execution.

setup.model: The resumed agent receives useful history with a warning built into it: old approval60/v3, new request187.20/v4 and OP-6 still unknown.
The word “approved” hides the amount and policy that limited yesterday’s permission. Resuming a conversation does not settle today’s action.

repair.refresh: Current evidence and exact approval conditions are now compared with the new action. Old authority is not silently stretched to the larger amount.
repair.status: The unresolved earlier operation now gets its own status investigation. Another refund must not be inferred from an unanswered request.

setup.status: OP-6’s unknown effect is the detail the short summary dropped. Losing that fact can make a repeated payment look like a fresh action.

repair.brief: The small working brief now keeps exact amounts, scoped approval, unknown effects and source pointers. Shorter context does not require losing decisive facts.

setup.brief: The brief contains supported booking work but still lacks payment evidence. A summary that says complete would conceal that partial investigation.

repair.review: The handoff now names the missing decision and owner. Limited review capacity produces an explicit pending state, not automatic permission.

setup.review: Not every dated detail needs another full investigation. The new stale narrative fact cannot change the action, authority or unknown payment outcome.

repair.refresh: Refresh effort now follows decision relevance. Unaffected verified work is retained while policy, approval and OP-6 still receive the checks they need.

as-01-action-service.screen: Shows the case and collects the requested help
as-01-action-service.backend: Runs the workflow and handles proposed actions
as-01-action-service.claude: Proposes a tool call or explains the evidence
as-01-action-service.orders: Stores order facts and applicable credit rules
as-01-action-service.gate: Checks whether this proposed action is permitted
as-01-action-service.tools: Describe available actions and their accepted inputs
as-01-action-service.session: Identifies the signed-in account from trusted state
as-01-action-service.payment: Performs a submitted credit and reports its status
as-01-action-service.ledger: Keeps operation identity, status and observed receipts
as-01-action-service.human: Reviews a proposal needing a person’s authority

as-02-document-pipeline.source: Provides the original invoice and its identity
as-02-document-pipeline.worker: Takes a file and runs its intake steps
as-02-document-pipeline.extract: Proposes invoice fields from the supplied document
as-02-document-pipeline.check: Checks field structure and agreement with evidence
as-02-document-pipeline.ledger: Keeps each file’s progress and outcome separate
as-02-document-pipeline.review: Resolves unclear or unreadable source evidence

as-03-grounded-assistant.ask: Provides the machine question and user scope
as-03-grounded-assistant.search: Finds applicable passages within the permitted scope
as-03-grounded-assistant.answer: Explains supplied evidence and names its sources
as-03-grounded-assistant.catalog: Identifies manuals and exposes readable content
as-03-grounded-assistant.guard: Checks access and separates evidence from instructions
as-03-grounded-assistant.owner: Decides which unresolved operating instruction governs

as-04-research-system.request: Defines the decision, constraints and expected result
as-04-research-system.coord: Coordinates investigation and combines its evidence
as-04-research-system.special: Investigates a bounded question using supplied context
as-04-research-system.ledger: Tracks which required questions have usable evidence
as-04-research-system.owner: Approves the pilot’s actual scope and budget

as-05-code-change.request: Defines how missing and zero deposits must differ
as-05-code-change.code: Shows implementation, callers and existing examples
as-05-code-change.claude: Investigates relevant code and proposes a scoped change
as-05-code-change.rules: Supplies relevant conventions and reusable procedures
as-05-code-change.tests: Checks observed behavior against expected outcomes
as-05-code-change.owner: Reviews the proposal and controls its release

as-06-ci-review.packet: Supplies changed code, requirements and test evidence
as-06-ci-review.model: Proposes defects with a location and consequence
as-06-ci-review.gate: Checks run success and usable output structure
as-06-ci-review.integration: Checks findings against combined code behavior
as-06-ci-review.ledger: Tracks current findings and their earlier status
as-06-ci-review.post: Publishes checked findings within granted permissions

as-07-work-queue.jobs: Provides each job’s deadline and evidence needs
as-07-work-queue.route: Chooses a processing lane for those requirements
as-07-work-queue.live: Runs the waiting interaction and its local tools
as-07-work-queue.batch: Processes supplied independent requests for later results
as-07-work-queue.ledger: Matches each result to its source and outcome
as-07-work-queue.recover: Chooses recovery from the failure and effect risk

as-08-resumable-case.saved: Stores dated facts, approval scope and pending work
as-08-resumable-case.model: Builds a current investigation from available evidence
as-08-resumable-case.refresh: Checks relevant changes and the current action’s authority
as-08-resumable-case.status: Looks up what the earlier operation actually did
as-08-resumable-case.brief: Keeps exact critical facts in a smaller working view
as-08-resumable-case.review: Owns unresolved decisions and visible review overflow
